chunks: And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Abi al-Şuhban, from Muhammad ibn Bakr ibn Janah, from Ali ibn Shajara, from Bashir al-Nabbal, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about fasting the Day of Doubt, so he said: 'Fast it, for if it is from Sha'ban it is voluntary (fasting of supererogation), and if it is from the month of Ramadan, then it is a day for which you were enabled (to fast).'

key_terms.شَعْبَانَ: Sha'ban (the eighth month of the Islamic calendar)
key_terms.صَوْمِ يَوْمِ الشَّكِّ: Fasting of the Day of Doubt

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on fasting on the Day of Doubt (Yawm al-Shakk) in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the principle of *ihtiyat* (precaution) in lunar calendar calculations, reflecting the Shia reliance on the Imams' guidance during periods of astronomical uncertainty. By framing the fast as potentially voluntary or obligatory, the Imam provides a flexible jurisprudential solution that safeguards the integrity of Ramadan worship while acknowledging the practical realities of moon sighting. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on following the Imam's directive to avoid missing obligatory acts due to doubt.
